description: UAE Dubai Health Authority (DHA) and Department of Health Abu Dhabi (DOH) Essential Benefits Package (EBP) — mandatory minimum coverage for all health insurance policies issued in the UAE. Non-compliant exclusions or copay structures are void and unenforceable under UAE Law No. 11 of 2013.

clauses.title: Mandatory Essential Benefits — Inpatient Coverage
clauses.full_text: All health insurance policies in Dubai must cover inpatient treatment including surgical and medical care, room and board at a standard ward or semi-private room level, ICU care, diagnostic investigations, medications prescribed during hospitalization, physiotherapy directly related to the admission, and blood transfusions. Coverage must be provided for all network hospitals approved by DHA. Exclusion of inpatient care for acute medical conditions is not permitted.

clauses.title: Mandatory Outpatient Coverage
clauses.full_text: Outpatient general practitioner and specialist consultations must be covered with a maximum copayment of 20% of the eligible claim amount and not to exceed AED 50 per consultation. Diagnostic services including laboratory tests and basic radiology (X-ray) must be included within the EBP with a maximum copay of 20% up to AED 50 per visit. Any copay exceeding AED 50 per outpatient visit is prohibited under the EBP.
clauses.regulatory_note: DHA Health Insurance Law No. 11 of 2013; Executive Council Resolution No. 32 of 2013

clauses.title: Mandatory Emergency Treatment — Worldwide
clauses.full_text: Emergency treatment must be covered at any facility globally without prior authorization. Within the UAE, emergency treatment at non-network facilities must be reimbursed at network rates. Insurers may not deny emergency claims on the grounds of lack of pre-authorization. Post-emergency notification within 24 hours of admission is acceptable. Copay must not apply to genuine emergency admissions.
clauses.regulatory_note: DHA EBP Circular 15/2014, Section 4.3 — Emergency services cannot be denied for non-authorization

clauses.title: Mandatory Maternity Benefits
clauses.full_text: Health insurance policies must cover maternity benefits including normal delivery, caesarean section, antenatal consultations (minimum 6 visits), and postnatal care. Maternity waiting period must not exceed 12 months. Newborn care for the first 30 days from birth must be included without additional premium. The EBP prohibits exclusion of pregnancy-related complications.
clauses.regulatory_note: DHA Circular 33/2015 — maternity waiting period cap enforcement

clauses.title: Mandatory Pharmacy Coverage
clauses.full_text: Prescribed medications for covered conditions must be covered with a maximum copayment of 30% for brand-name medications and 20% for generics. The EBP requires coverage of medications listed on the UAE Ministry of Health formulary. Medications prescribed during a covered inpatient stay must be covered at 100% with no additional copay.

clauses.title: Mandatory Copayment Caps — EBP Maximum
clauses.full_text: The Essential Benefits Package mandates the following maximum copayment caps which no insurer may exceed: Outpatient consultation: 20% of eligible amount, maximum AED 50 per visit. Emergency services: AED 0 (no copay). Inpatient admission: maximum AED 500 per admission (flat copay). Annual out-of-pocket maximum for EBP benefits: AED 10,000 per member per year. Any policy applying copay amounts above these regulatory caps renders the excess amount void and the insurer is liable for the difference.
clauses.regulatory_note: Executive Council Resolution 32/2013, Article 14 — Financial obligations of insured persons

clauses.title: Prohibited Annual Limit Below EBP Minimum
clauses.full_text: All health insurance policies in the UAE must provide a minimum annual benefit limit of AED 150,000 per member per year for Essential Benefits Package coverage. Policies may not impose annual sub-limits on individual EBP benefits (emergency, maternity, inpatient acute) below the following minimums: Emergency worldwide: AED 150,000 per incident; Maternity: AED 7,000 (normal), AED 10,000 (caesarean); Inpatient per admission: AED 150,000. Policies with annual limits below AED 150,000 are non-compliant.
clauses.regulatory_note: DHA Health Insurance Law No. 11 of 2013, Article 8 — minimum coverage thresholds

clauses.title: Prohibited Exclusions — Conditions Insurers May Not Exclude
clauses.full_text: The following conditions and treatments may not be excluded from coverage under any EBP-compliant policy in the UAE: (a) HIV/AIDS treatment if member is a legal resident with valid visa; (b) Mental health acute inpatient treatment — up to 15 days per year must be covered; (c) Substance abuse detoxification — up to 7 days per year; (d) Cancer screening tests per MOH guidelines; (e) Dialysis for end-stage renal disease; (f) Physiotherapy directly related to a covered inpatient admission. Any policy clause purporting to exclude these is void and unenforceable under UAE Law.
clauses.regulatory_note: DHA Ministerial Resolution 52/2018 — Prohibited exclusions under EBP

clauses.title: Mandatory Limits on Waiting Periods
clauses.full_text: Waiting periods for pre-existing conditions under EBP-compliant policies may not exceed 6 months from the date of continuous coverage. Insurers may not impose any waiting period (including initial 30-day waiting periods) for: emergency treatment, maternity complications, and cancer treatment for newly diagnosed conditions. Transfer of coverage between approved insurers must carry over waiting period completion — insurers may not restart waiting periods for transferred members.
clauses.regulatory_note: DHA Circular 15/2014 Section 5 — Waiting period restrictions and portability
